title: Valid Palindrome
statement:
A phrase is a palindrome if, after you throw away everything that isn't a letter or a digit and ignore the difference between upper and lower case, it reads the same forwards and backwards. Given a string `s`, return `True` if it is a palindrome in that sense and `False` otherwise.

If nothing is left after throwing characters away (for example a string of only punctuation and spaces), the empty remainder counts as a palindrome. Digits are compared as characters, so "0" and "P" are different.

Constraints: 1 <= len(s) <= 2 * 10^5; `s` contains printable ASCII characters.

examples.explanation: Keeping only the letters and ignoring case leaves "steponnopets", which reads the same in both directions.
Every character is punctuation or a space, so nothing remains to disagree; the empty remainder counts as a palindrome.

hints: Which characters actually matter here, and which should your comparison never look at?
You could build a cleaned copy of the string and compare it to its reverse. Can you compare characters from the two ends directly instead?
With pointers at both ends, what should you do when one of them points at a character that is not a letter or digit?
Try "0P" and "ab_a". Which comparisons would be wrong if you treated '0' like 'P' or kept the underscore?
Two pointers moving inward: skip non-alphanumeric characters on each side, compare the rest case-insensitively, and stop when they meet.
followUps: What are the time and space complexity, and what does building a cleaned copy cost compared with the two-pointer approach?
How would your solution change for Unicode text with accents or characters from other scripts?
How would you allow at most one character to be deleted and still call the string a palindrome?
What does your code do on a string of only punctuation, and is that the right answer?
idealAnswerPoints: Keeps only letters and digits and compares case-insensitively
Uses two pointers moving inward, skipping non-alphanumeric characters, for O(1) extra space
Treats an empty remainder as a palindrome and handles odd and even lengths with the same loop
States O(n) time and O(1) space, noting the cleaned-copy version uses O(n) space
weakAnswerSigns: Compares the raw string to its reverse without cleaning it first
Lower-cases or filters in a way that treats digits and letters as equal, or keeps underscores
Moves the pointers without bounds checks and indexes out of range on strings of punctuation

rubric.correctness: Correct on mixed case, punctuation, spaces, digits, underscores, single characters and punctuation-only strings.
rubric.efficiency: O(n) time; the two-pointer version is O(1) space, while a cleaned copy at O(n) space is acceptable if named.
rubric.code_quality: Readable condition ordering inside the loop, built-in isalnum/lower rather than hand-written ranges.
rubric.communication: Explains which characters are skipped, why '0' and 'P' differ, and the choice between a copy and two pointers.
